clue.text: Stock-market method accountants help bear

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, so several are CAS
to give a hand is to help
to bear a load is to carry it

explanation.surface: A trading technique on the exchange: accountants lending support to a bearish dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock-market' suggests shares, but here it is a market for stock: a wholesale warehouse where traders pay on the spot and take goods away themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesale trading system in which buyers pay at once and remove the goods themselves is a way of running a stock market.

clue.text: Normal fare for one of the estates

explanation.surface: Everyday food served to a member of one of the realm's estates.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commons, the elected House, represents the third estate of the realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary shared provisions at a college are its daily rations; the elected lower House of Parliament stands for the third estate.

clue.text: Dawn of new day for students' union

definitions.text: Dawn of new day for students' union

parts.words: Dawn of new day for students' union
parts.note: reads as the start of something fresh for a student body, but describes sunrise; NUS, the National Union of Students, rearranged gives the first part

explanation.surface: A fresh start is beginning for the student body.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a cryptic description: NUS (National Union of Students) made new gives SUN, and students at university are said to be UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is the moment the sun rises above the horizon.

clue.text: It adds up to a concrete contribution

explanation.surface: Something that totals into a solid donation.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand total is what figures add up to; crushed stone or gravel mixed with cement is a component of concrete.

clue.text: Influence, some say, of old penny newspaper

parts.note: D stood for the pre-decimal penny (Latin denarius)
a rag is a slang term for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A cheap paper costing an old penny is said to sway opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' marks the definition as slang: in American usage pull or clout is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, having pull or clout with powerful people is described with this word.

clue.text: Palatial music-hall

parts.note: names both the Moorish palace in Granada and the grand London variety theatre that borrowed its name

explanation.surface: A grand variety theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: A famous London music hall in Leicester Square took its name from the Moorish palace at Granada.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a Moorish royal palace in Spain and to a celebrated London variety theatre.

clue.text: Chief article used for lining

explanation.surface: The boss's item for marking out lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief or sovereign governs; a straight-edged measuring strip is used to draw straight lines.

clue.text: Compact sort of pancake

explanation.surface: A dense little griddle cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat powder case is a dated name for a make-up compact; the word also names a thick griddle cake.

clue.text: State to care about, in short

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for South Carolina, a US state

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of care are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to state, briefly, that you care about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns CARE into ARCE, placed after SC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in short supply is rare or hard to come by.

clue.text: Treatise by Scotsman has no diagram

parts.note: mon is a Scots form of man
O as a nought or zero stands for none
a graph is a type of diagram

explanation.surface: A Scottish author writes a scholarly work without any illustrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly study of a single subject is a kind of treatise.

clue.text: Bloomer left Jill and Jack in extremely reduced circumstances

indicators.note: the names are reduced at their extremes, losing first and last letters

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme couple fallen on very hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is something that blooms. Jill and Jack shorn of their ends give IL and AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering shrub with fragrant purple blossom is a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Bird giving no quarter in active display

parts.note: O as a nought stands for none

indicators.note: in places the quarter inside the word for active

parts.note: spry means lively and active
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A bird putting on an energetic show without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no quarter' reads as a single phrase meaning no mercy, but it splits into O and a compass point E.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish-eating hawk is a bird of prey.

clue.text: Fractionally above one? That's not right

explanation.surface: Something a bit over one, which is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction whose numerator exceeds its denominator has a value above one; anything unseemly or incorrect is not right.

clue.text: Maps out article on boat

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of maps are put out of order

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone sets out charts and a document on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed skiff from China and the Far East is a type of boat.

clue.text: Duck "a l'orange'?

parts.note: reads as a French dish but names a species of duck that shares its name with a small orange

explanation.surface: Duck served with orange sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: One word names both an ornamental Asian duck and a small citrus fruit, so it is a duck that is also an orange.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a brightly coloured Asian duck and to a loose-skinned citrus fruit.

clue.text: See cheat pinch point in game

parts.note: to crib is to cheat by copying
to bag is slang for to steal or pinch
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Watch a card-player cheating by stealing a point during play.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game scored with pegs on a board is a game.

clue.text: Frenchwoman's sauce

parts.note: the dressing named for a woman of the Béarn region in south-west France

explanation.surface: A sauce made by a French cook.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is also the feminine form for a native of Béarn, a former province of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich egg-and-butter sauce flavoured with tarragon is named after the Béarn region, and the feminine noun means a woman from there.

clue.text: Select but not exclusive

parts.note: describes choosing from many sources rather than one, the paradox of being choosy yet broad

explanation.surface: Choosy, yet open to all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who picks the best from a wide range of sources selects without excluding whole schools.

clue.text: This clue is one such example of syntax

definitions.text: This clue is one such example of syntax

parts.words: This clue is one such example of syntax
parts.note: the clue points at itself: a grammatical string of words with subject and verb

explanation.surface: A self-referential remark about grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatically complete group of words with subject and verb is a unit of syntax.

clue.text: Throws up part as provincial governor

indicators.note: in a down clue, throwing up means the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: An official vomits partly.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Persia, the ruler of a province was a governor appointed by the king.

clue.text: A lot of money for a boat

explanation.surface: A fortune spent on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a fortune is making a large sum; a mail steamer on a regular route was a packet boat.

clue.text: On that account the rate has end misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced means the letter is taken out of its position and put elsewhere

parts.note: the end of rate is its final letter E

explanation.surface: Because of that, a rate's last figure was put in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' shifts the E of RATE forward to make REAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning because of that or for that reason.

clue.text: Hand over the change

explanation.surface: Give someone their change.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something to another person is to hand it over; a move from one place or job to another is a change.

clue.text: Type of heating for medieval chamber

explanation.surface: A heating system for an old room.
explanation.definitionFit: Heating powered by the sun is one type; an upper private room in a medieval house was so called.

clue.text: Total has not been doctored

explanation.surface: The whole thing has been left untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: Total means whole; a horse not castrated is described as whole, never neutered by a vet.

clue.text: Harden fury about letter from Greece

indicators.note: about means the word for fury goes around the Greek letter

parts.note: ire is anger or fury
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Anger hardens around a message from Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: To accustom someone to hardship is to toughen them.

clue.text: Indian religious system died away

indicators.note: away means the letter for died is sent off

parts.note: a creed is a system of religious belief

explanation.surface: A faith from the subcontinent has faded out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' suggests the subcontinent, but it is a Native American people of Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American people of the Canadian plains and woodlands.

clue.text: Tempestuous spirit of Belinda's guardian angel

explanation.surface: A stormy ghost watching over a woman named Belinda.
explanation.walkthrough: The airy sprite in Shakespeare's The Tempest shares a name with Belinda's sylph in Pope's The Rape of the Lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero's airy servant in The Tempest and the sylph protecting Belinda in Pope's poem share this name.

clue.text: Put rude construction on concealing it for badness

indicators.note: concealing means the reworked letters hide the word it inside them
putting a construction on words means reworking them, so the letters of put rude are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone puts a rude interpretation on something hiding its wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' turns PUTRUDE into TURPUDE, and 'concealing' tucks IT into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Depravity or wickedness is moral badness.

clue.text: Nutrient not much needed

parts.note: describes a mineral the body requires only in tiny amounts, with not much read as a small quantity

explanation.surface: A food component that hardly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerals such as zinc or iron that the body needs in minute quantities are required in small amounts.
